title: 3D Model Generation of Penicillium Spores Using Slice-and-View
content: Volume microscopy is a popular technique in the biological sciences that involves generating 3D models of samples. Methods include imaging serial sections of a sample by slicing it with a microtome or milling with a focused ion beam (FIB), a process known as slice-and-view [1]. The acquired image stack is processed in an external software to generate 3D models that reveal information about the sample, such as structure and scale. We used a FIB to create models of ungerminated Penicillium spores. The genesis of the project was to investigate questions about their morphology. In conjunction with this question, the secondary purpose was to develop the slice-and-view technique and establish a functional SOP.
